speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry will provide an update on the study into a ban on electric collars for animal training; and (b) whether the Ministry will study the enforcement mechanisms for the Guidelines for Rehoming and Adoption of Dogs developed by the Rehoming and Adoption Workgroup.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just check what concerns the Ministry has in terms of coming up with a ban on the use of electric collars?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think Senior Minister of State Tan himself tried the use of the electrical collar and it is painful.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Obviously, it is painful for the dogs as well and that is why it is being used to train them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, how could it not be a physical abuse when it causes pain and suffering to the dogs which are being trained?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I did not post about it, but as part of the whole process, I did indeed get my NParks colleagues to bring in a range of electric collars and I tried all of them on myself.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On a range for one to 10 in terms of spectrum, I probably got to about seven and it has been very painful.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is not just the pain, but also the shock of it because the animal or whoever is wearing the electric collar would not know when the shock is applied.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, I can empathise with what the Member is saying and I also shared the position the Government is taking on to look at some of these issues in my reply to his question.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, I must commend the Member for his doggedness.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On 4 November 2020 as well as 4 March 2022, I have made some elaborations on our considerations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But more importantly, in the coming months, we will release the guidelines and we will welcome a further conversation among different segments of our community – the dog owners, pet owners, trainers, animal welfare groups and other members of the public.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, we will continue with this conversation; and the guidelines will be out very soon.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But more importantly, the point the Member is making is about unnecessary pain and animal cruelty.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For the remaining cases, our investigations showed that most arose from disputes – disamenities caused by pets or community animals, or involved the deaths of community animals which could be due to non-cruelty-related reasons such as accidental fall from heights, fights among community animals or road traffic accidents.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The community has a crucial role to play because each case is a case too many.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Pet owners can refer to the Code of Animal Welfare for pet owners to learn about the minimal standards expected for animal housing, management and care.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We urge anyone with information and/or evidence on suspected animal cruelty cases to promptly share it with AVS via our website or calling our Animal Response Centre at our hotline.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The timeliness of information is critical to enable us to establish the cause of death.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: AVS will continue to work closely with stakeholders such as animal welfare groups to raise public awareness on responsible interactions with animals.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As you all know, Senior Minister of State Tan loves animals.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I am sure whatever he says, he will personally look into it.
